A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DPCore and provide readable methods, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. The reorganized appendix material can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: v3 reports original classification and segmentation experiments on four benchmarks, together with component ablations and analyses of changing domain streams.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds results for RDumb and fixed-size coreset strategies.

M1.justification: v4 Section 5.3 adds optional coreset management procedures that discard the oldest prompt or merge the most similar prompts when a size limit is exceeded. The default dynamically growing coreset, adaptation objective, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four benchmarks and retain CSC, CDC, CDC-2D, PTTA, small-batch, and STL10 reference-data evaluations. The new coreset-cap experiment changes a model configuration within existing ImageNet-C coverage.

E2.justification: v4 Table 1 adds RDumb to the ImageNet-C CSC comparison. Existing comparator memberships in the other matched experiments are retained; the newly discussed PeTTA is not evaluated.

E3.justification: v4 Table 5 introduces a K=15 coreset constraint and compares discard and merge policies against flexible coreset growth across ten domain orders. Existing benchmark models, corruption severity, batch sizes, optimization settings, and validation procedures are retained.

E4.justification: The new fixed-size coreset study tests the accuracy cost of limiting memory and whether merging preserves knowledge better than discarding. Existing ablations and robustness analyses are retained. Appendix F.1 adds explanatory discussion rather than a new failure-case experiment.

E5.justification: The ten-order CSC evaluation and ten-pattern CDC-2D mean and standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged. The new memory comparison extends the existing averaging practice without introducing new seed information, uncertainty estimates, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: v4 adds RDumb's 44.6% mean error and capped-coreset errors of 42.3% for discarding and 41.1% for merging, alongside the retained flexible-coreset result of 40.2%. Table 3 corrects Exp-3's gain from +8.7 to +10.7, retaining its 45.1% error. Table 4 changes ViDA's parameter count from 7.13M to 93.70M, clarifying that 7.13M counts additional parameters. Other matched benchmark and appendix results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives, well-separated-cluster assumption, and three propositions and proofs are retained. v3 Appendix C.4 becomes v4 Appendix B.4; punctuation and numbering changes do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about CDC, DPCore's three components, classification and segmentation performance, and computational efficiency. The added evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v3 identifies mixed-domain batches as an unresolved limitation. v4 Appendix F.1 explains how unstable batch statistics could repeatedly trigger new prompts and increase computation, drawing an analogy to the existing Table 3 Exp-2. The new memory study also interprets merging as preferable to discarding under a fixed cap.

D1.justification: v4 updates the advertised code location from zybeich/DPCore to yunbeizhang/DPCore and adds an RDumb implementation link in Appendix A.2. It also clarifies ViDA's total versus additional parameter counts. DPCore's main implementation hyperparameters are unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds targeted comparisons with PeTTA's memory components and RDumb's resets, plus a short continual-learning subsection and additional citations. These broaden the context while retaining the central positioning around managing domain groups under CDC.

P1.justification: Related work moves from v3 Appendix A into a revised main-text Section 2, and the appendix background and baseline sections are consolidated. v4 also adds a failure-case subsection, acknowledgments, and affiliation edits. Most method, experimental, theoretical, and concluding prose is retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds the fixed-size coreset Table 5 and an RDumb row in Table 1. Existing tables and figures are repositioned as the document reflows, with cross-reference styling changes. All six figures retain their graphical content.

improvement.justification: v4 makes the memory–accuracy tradeoff assessable through the new capped-coreset study: 41.1–42.3% error versus 40.2% with flexible growth. The RDumb comparison, corrected reporting in Tables 3–4, and more specific failure-case discussion improve completeness and clarity. These are limited gains because the core benchmark findings and theoretical support remain unchanged.
